label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents a sizable group of respondents (n = 332) characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Scores on the UCLA-8 loneliness scale (mean ≈ 1.24), PHQ-9 depression scale (mean ≈ 0.81), and GAD-7 anxiety scale (mean ≈ 0.84) all fall well below clinical thresholds, indicating generally positive psychological well-being. These individuals are highly educated males who engage in moderate daily screen or internet use (1–3 hours).
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Low loneliness scores suggesting strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology well below clinical concern
Very low anxiety levels indicating effective emotional regulation
Moderate and controlled screen/internet usage (1–3 hours daily)
High educational attainment potentially linked to stable socioeconomic conditions
tone: Stable, socially connected, and psychologically resilient

label: High-Distress Heavy-Screen-Use Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures female respondents with graduate-level education or above who spend more than 5 hours daily on screens. They report elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean 1.71), notable depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean 1.73), and markedly high anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean 2.18). The co-occurrence of all three distress indicators at above-average levels suggests a pattern of compounded psychological burden, potentially linked to extended screen time and the pressures associated with advanced education.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Exhibits the highest distress on the GAD-7 anxiety measure among the three indicators
Engages in heavy daily screen use (more than 5 hours)
Represents a sizable subgroup (n=181) suggesting this is not a rare pattern
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety in a high-screen-use, highly educated female population
